assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Catalyst
items.clue: A substance that speeds up a reaction without being used up.

items.label: Rusting
items.clue: The slow change of iron into a flaky brown oxide in damp air

items.label: Effervescence
items.clue: Bubbles of gas being given off in a liquid during a reaction

items.label: Rearrangement
items.clue: Atoms separating and then joining up again in a different pattern

questions.stem: Which statement about the pH scale is correct?

options.text: Higher numbers are more acidic
Neutral solutions have a pH of 0
Lower numbers are more acidic
All acids have exactly the same pH

questions.explanation: Yes. The lower the pH below 7, the more acidic the solution. pH 7 is neutral and above 7 is alkaline.

questions.stem: Universal indicator is green at pH 7, blue at pH 9 and purple at pH 13. A cleaner turns it blue. What does this show?

options.text: It is more alkaline than purple liquids
It is as alkaline as a purple liquid
It is harmless, as it is not acidic
It is less alkaline than a purple liquid

questions.explanation: Yes. Blue means about pH 9, which is alkaline but less alkaline than pH 13 (purple). The higher the pH above 7, the more alkaline.

questions.stem: Blue litmus paper is dipped into a solution and stays blue. What does this show?

options.text: It is not acidic, as an acid turns it red
It is alkaline, as blue means alkali
It is acidic, as acids turn litmus blue
It is neutral, as nothing changed

questions.explanation: Yes. Acids turn blue litmus red. Blue litmus stays blue in both neutral and alkaline solutions, so you only know the solution is not acidic.

questions.stem: Solution X has pH 2 and solution Y has pH 5. Which statement is correct?

options.text: Y is the more acidic of the two
X is more strongly acidic than Y
X is acidic but Y is an alkali
X and Y are both weak alkalis

questions.explanation: Both are acidic (below pH 7); the lower the pH, the more strongly acidic the solution.

questions.stem: Litmus shows whether a solution is acidic or alkaline. What extra information does universal indicator give?

options.text: How strongly acidic or alkaline it is
The name of the acid or alkali in it
How many grams of acid it contains
Whether the liquid is safe to drink

questions.explanation: Universal indicator has a range of colours, so it shows the pH: how strongly acidic or alkaline.

questions.stem: A solution is tested with litmus. Red litmus paper stays red and blue litmus paper stays blue. What is the solution?

options.text: Acidic, as the red paper stayed red
Alkaline, as the blue paper stayed blue
Neutral, with a pH of around 0
Neutral, with a pH close to 7

questions.explanation: An acid would turn blue litmus red and an alkali would turn red litmus blue; no change means neutral.

questions.stem: An alkali is added slowly to an acid of pH 2. What happens to the pH of the mixture?

options.text: It falls from 2 to about 0
It rises from 2 towards 7
It stays at 2 the whole time
It jumps straight from 2 to 14

questions.explanation: The alkali neutralises the acid, so the mixture becomes less acidic and the pH rises towards 7.

questions.stem: Red cabbage juice is red in vinegar, purple in water and green in soapy water. Why can it be used as an indicator?

options.text: It turns acids and alkalis into water
It dissolves well in both acids and alkalis
It has a strong colour that stains liquids
It has different colours in acids and alkalis

questions.explanation: An indicator is a substance whose colour depends on whether it is in an acid or an alkali.

questions.stem: Universal indicator is added to a solution of pH 1. What colour does it turn, and why?

options.text: Red, as it is strongly acidic
Yellow, as it is weakly acidic
Green, as it is close to neutral
Purple, as it is strongly alkaline

questions.explanation: pH 1 is strongly acidic, and universal indicator is red in strongly acidic solutions.
